problem_statement: Northwind Studio is a multi-page marketing site built on this Angular 17 agency template (a Home landing surface, plus About, Services and Pricing pages, all under a shared top navigation and a footer that renders on every route). The studio wants a small, consistent 'Launch readiness' rail to sit in the footer of every marketing surface: a labelled row of the launch phase chips (Draft copy, Design review, Build & wire, QA pass, Go live) plus a live 'Readiness view' readout with a toggle that tells the team whether the board is currently in the planning view or the shipping view. The phases are read differently under each view, so the rail should always name the view the board is set to. Ship the Launch readiness rail so it (1) appears in the footer on the Home, About and Services surfaces alike, (2) lays out its phase-chip row responsively without horizontal overflow on a phone, (3) matches the studio's teal-and-coral accent styling (dashed teal/coral chips, not an off-palette dark slab), and (4) keeps the 'Readiness view' readout in sync with the toggle so a lead who switches to the shipping view sees the readout update to 'shipping'. Keep the rest of the site — the top navigation, the page headings, the marketing copy, the imagery, the production Angular build — intact with no console or network errors.
required_content: Add a shared 'Launch readiness' rail to the marketing footer so it renders on the Home, About and Services surfaces (a shared standalone component invoked from the app-footer, not a per-page copy).
The rail shows a 'Launch readiness' label, a chip row of the phase tags (Draft copy, Design review, Build & wire, QA pass, Go live), and a 'Readiness view' readout with a toggle.
The phase-chip row must wrap responsively so no marketing surface overflows horizontally on a 390px phone (overflow tolerance 24px).
Style the rail in the studio's teal-and-coral accent language (dashed teal/coral accent chips), consistent and legible, not an off-palette dark slab.

Wire the 'Readiness view' readout to the readiness-view toggle: after clicking the toggle, the readout must read 'shipping' when the board is set to the shipping view — it must re-read the live readiness mode, not show a stale captured value.
Preserve the top navigation, the page headings, the marketing copy, the imagery and the production Angular build with no console or network errors.
author_notes: Built on the AndrewJBateman angular-website-example Angular 17 multi-page marketing template (the Namari agency layout: top navigation, hero banner, About / Services / Pricing routes and a shared footer), rebranded to Northwind Studio. The shared Launch readiness rail is rendered from the app-footer and reuses the studio's own teal accent (#16b7b7) and coral accent (#f0655a) with the banner and logo image assets; the Open Sans web font is vendored locally so no remote assets are fetched. The responsive phase-chip layout, the teal/coral palette styling, the visual hierarchy and the readiness-view interaction wiring were designed by hand for this marketing site, not bulk-generated. The design keywords guiding it were a wrapping responsive chip layout, a teal-and-coral accent palette, a legible typographic hierarchy, and a consistent footer rail spanning every route.
design_constraints: Implement the Launch readiness rail as a shared standalone component rendered from the footer so a single source of truth reaches every marketing surface; do not paste divergent copies per page or build a detached widget.
The phase-chip row must use a fluid, wrapping responsive layout (no fixed-width nowrap track) so it never forces horizontal overflow on tablet or mobile; the chip spacing must stay legible.

The rail must adopt the studio's teal-and-coral accent palette, dashed-accent chip style and typography so it reads as part of Northwind Studio, not a foreign block; keep it consistent with the site's own image and logo assets.
The 'Readiness view' readout must reflect the CURRENT readiness mode after every toggle by reading the live data-ready-mode attribute, so it can never go stale relative to the visible palette.
Do not remove or regress the top navigation, the page headings, the marketing copy, the imagery or the production Angular build.

change_completion: The Launch readiness rail is present in the footer of the Home, About and Services surfaces (the shared component reaches all three routes).
After clicking the readiness-view toggle on Home, the 'Readiness view' readout updates to 'shipping' — the post-interaction terminal state changed from 'planning'.
design_consistency: The rail on the footer states matches the reference's teal/coral styling under the visual-regression gate (pixel/ssim/block-fidelity), not an off-palette dark slab.
The rail adopts the studio's teal-and-coral dashed-accent idiom so it reads as part of Northwind Studio across the marketing surfaces.
responsive: No captured marketing surface overflows horizontally beyond 24px on a 390px phone; the phase-chip row wraps.
desktop_footer_home, mobile_footer_home and mobile_initial keep the Launch readiness rail readable across viewports without clipping or overflow.
regression: The top navigation and the page headings remain present and functional.
The marketing copy, the imagery and the production Angular build are not removed or broken, with no console or network errors.

state_constraints: desktop_initial, tablet_initial and mobile_initial protect the rebranded Home landing and responsive shell.
desktop_about, mobile_about and desktop_services protect the existing marketing surfaces and carry the Launch readiness rail in the footer.
desktop_footer_home and mobile_footer_home scroll the Launch readiness rail into view and must show the teal/coral rail without horizontal overflow.
desktop_footer_about and desktop_footer_services protect the rail's presence on the About and Services footers.
tablet_footer_home protects the rail's tablet layout without overflow.
toggle_ready_home clicks the readiness-view toggle; the 'Readiness view' readout must then read 'shipping'.
